newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African fund managers' appetite for industrial shares pushed stocks higher, hoisting the index above the 8,000 level for first time in two months.
But shares finished off the day's peaks after players seized the opportunity to take some profits, dealers said.
"People liked the levels the shares got to and began selling them off their highs," one dealer said.
The industrial index finished up 57.2 points at 8,001.4 -- its best closing level since November 28 last year when it ended at 8,000.4.

During morning dealings, traders said investment funds had been evident in the market snapping up industrial stocks, notably blue-chips, after managers had drawn up strategies for the year. Sought-after shares included Sasol, SA Breweries, Richemont and Safren.
Arbitrage trading between the futures and spot market also raised shares as futures were sold and the underlying stocks bought. The industrial March futures contract was last at 7,873/80 from 7,810.
Dealers predicted a third consecutive day of gains for industrial stocks on Thursday.
Volumes were high after a lethargic holiday and early new year period with shares worth 694 million rand changing hands on Wednesday, traders said.

But activity had slowed a bit during the afternoon amid concerns about December gold and foreign exchange reserve figures due for release at 1600 GMT and expected to show a slight drop from November's 10.93 billion rand.

Dealers said a 60 million rand share swap between a South African and U.S. institution which had taken place late on Tuesday had boosted market sentiment as it showed renewed foreign confidence in local stocks.
Over 400,000 Sasol shares were involved in the swap, they said. Sasol ended the day steady at 55.50 rand after 895,400 shares worth over 49.5 million rand changed hands.
South Africa's exchange control regulations were liberalised in June last year and local institutions are now allowed to swap up to 10 percent of their local assets for offshore investments.
Amongst other shares on the Johannesburg bourse on Wednesday SA Breweries rose 175 cents to 119.50 rand, Remgro lifted 40 cents to 42 rand but Richemont shed 25 cents to 65 rand.
Gold shares drifted lower amid a lack of interest and as bullion's shaky downward run continued which saw the metal sink below the $356 level during the afternoon.
"The gold price is not helping stocks, nor is the (firmer) rand. People are nervous and not interested," a trader said.
The gold index ditched 14.0 points to a fresh year low of 1,398.7 after Vaal Reefs slid 700 cents to 278 rand, Freegold fell 75 cents to 32.25 and Dries lost 75 cents to 44.35 rand.
The March gold futures contract was at 975/85 from 985.
The spot market all-share index closed at 6,650.8, up 36.3 points with the all-share March futures contract at 6,215/25 from 6,195.
